subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity representation carries no H^n-mass off the support of the current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then H^n(M ∖ spt T) = 0, where spt T = U ∖ ⋃{W : W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, T vanishes on W} (Simon 6.2.11).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ T.support) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is the fact "μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0", used in step 2 of the parent proof (Simon 6.2.11 with 6.3.1; μ_T = θH^n⌞M by 6.3.2(3)).
1. Notation. M := R.carrier ⊆ U, θ := R.mult (θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By definition T.support = U ∖ Z with Z := T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲, where 𝒲 is the family of open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W (T ω = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Since M ⊆ U, M ∖ T.support = M ∩ Z.
2. Countable reduction. ℝ^P is second countable, so ⋃𝒲 = ⋃_k W_k for a countable subfamily (W_k) ⊆ 𝒲 (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable). By countable subadditivity it suffices to show H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 for one fixed W ∈ 𝒲.
3. A finite measure. C := closure W is compact and C ⊆ U, so ∫_{M ∩ C} θ dH^n < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞. Put ν := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C), a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
4. Orientation facts. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a plane Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, s ∈ {1, −1}. At such x: (a) |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm of the continuous alternating map, since |τ_i| = 1); (b) ξ(x) ≠ 0: the n-covector β_τ(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b} (for n = 0 the constant 1) is continuous, multilinear and alternating, and β_τ(τ) = det I = 1, so ξ(x)(β_τ) = s ≠ 0.
5. Testing T. Fix an n-covector α and set f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α). It is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for μ ≥ ν) and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ ν-a.e., so f_α ∈ L¹(ν). For every g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P, ℝ) with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω(x) := g(x)·α is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in W. As T vanishes on W and R represents T: 0 = T ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(g(x)α) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν (the integrand vanishes off W ⊆ C).
6. Fundamental lemma. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (open set W, measure ν, f_α locally integrable on W) gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M and ν is carried by M, ξ(x)(α) = 0 for ν-a.e. x ∈ W.
7. Conclusion. Let α_1, …, α_m be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P. Intersecting the finitely many full-measure sets of step 6, for ν-a.e. x ∈ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, hence ξ(x) = 0. By step 4(b), ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x. Therefore ν(W) = H^n(M ∩ C ∩ W) = H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, and by step 2, H^n(M ∖ T.support) = 0.
proof_key_steps: M ∖ spt T = M ∩ zeroRegion(T), a countable union of open W ⊂⊂ U on which T vanishes.
Testing T with g·α (g ∈ C_c^∞(W), α a constant covector) gives ∫ g θ ξ(α) dH^n⌞M = 0.
The fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations gives ξ = 0 a.e. on M ∩ W, while unit orientations are nonzero; hence H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.

subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); used in steps 3 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).

subproblems.title: The approximate tangent plane field of an integer multiplicity triple is measurable
subproblems.statement: For every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in a set U ⊆ ℝ^P (IMRep U n), the map x ↦ p_{T_xM}, the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x (the approximate tangent plane T_xM where it exists, {0} otherwise), is H^n⌞M-almost everywhere strongly measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3 §1 (T_xM is unique, 1.5(1)) and the definition 6.3.1 of an integer multiplicity current, in which ξ orients T_xM in an H^n-measurable way; this measurability is implicit in Simon's formulas ∫ div_M X dμ_V (Ch. 4, 2.2–2.7) used in steps 2, 5 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. a.e. identification. Let μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x. At such x the existential in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds, so approxTangentPlane n M x is some Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q'; by uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) Q' = Q_x.
2. Case n = 0. Every Q with finrank 0 equals ⊥, and approxTangentPlane 0 M x is ⊥ in both branches of its definition, so the map is the constant 0, which is strongly measurable. Assume n ≥ 1.
3. A unit simple n-vector determines its plane. Let ζ ∈ (Λ^n)^* with ζ(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, τ orthonormal, s = ±1. Claim: span τ = {v : ζ(ι_vβ) = 0 for every (n+1)-covector β}, where ι_vβ(u_1, …, u_n) := β(v, u_1, …, u_n). If v ∈ span τ then β(v, τ_1, …, τ_n) = 0 because the arguments are linearly dependent. If v ∉ span τ, let w := v − Σ_i⟨v, τ_i⟩τ_i ≠ 0 and β(u_0, …, u_n) := det(⟨c_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b=0..n} with c := (w, τ_1, …, τ_n), a continuous alternating (n+1)-form; the matrix (⟨c_a, (v, τ_1, …, τ_n)_b⟩) has first row (|w|², 0, …, 0) and lower-right block I_n, so β(v, τ) = |w|² and ζ(ι_vβ) = s|w|² ≠ 0. Consequently, if ζ orients both Q and Q' (IsUnitOrientationOf) then Q = Q'.
4. Continuity of the orientation-to-projection map. Let Ω := {(τ, s) : τ ∈ (ℝ^P)^n orthonormal, s ∈ {1, −1}}, a compact set, and Φ(τ, s) := (β ↦ s·β(τ)), a continuous map Ω → (Λ^n)^* (multilinear evaluation with |τ_i| = 1). Its image 𝒮 is compact, hence closed, and equals the set of ζ for which ∃ Q, IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q. The map G̃(τ, s) := Σ_i ⟨τ_i, ·⟩τ_i = starProjection(span τ) is continuous on Ω and, by step 3, constant on the fibres of Φ; hence G̃ = G∘Φ for a unique G : 𝒮 → End(ℝ^P). Since Φ : Ω → 𝒮 is a continuous surjection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space, it is a quotient map, so G is continuous on 𝒮. Extend G by 0 outside 𝒮; the extension is Borel measurable (𝒮 closed, G continuous on it).
5. Conclusion. For μ-a.e. x (step 1), ξ(x) = Φ(τ, s) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q_x = approxTangentPlane n M x, hence starProjection(approxTangentPlane n M x) = G(ξ(x)). Since ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and G is Borel, G∘ξ is μ-a.e. measurable; End(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional (second countable and metrizable), so G∘ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so is the μ-a.e. equal map x ↦ (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection.
proof_key_steps: Almost everywhere the approximate tangent plane is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (uniqueness of T_xM).
A unit simple n-vector determines its plane (kernel of v ↦ ζ(ι_v ·)).
The map unit simple n-vector ↦ projection is continuous on the compact set of such vectors (quotient-map argument); compose with the a.e.-measurable ξ.

subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors versus Gram determinants (Cauchy–Binet)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n: (1) for every n-covector α on ℝ^P and v_1, …, v_n ∈ ℝ^P, |α(v_1, …, v_n)| ≤ |α|_E·(det(v_i·v_j)_{i,j})^{1/2}, where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{i_1<⋯<i_n} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15; (2) for every orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n in ℝ^P there is an n-covector α with |α|_E ≤ 1 and α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), |α v| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α * Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)))) ∧ ∀ τ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∃ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ 1 ∧ α τ = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.1 (Λ^n with the inner product making e^{i_1}∧⋯∧e^{i_n} orthonormal, 6.1.15) and 6.3.4–3.5 (|v_1∧⋯∧v_n| = J); these are the algebraic facts behind "M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W}θ dH^n" (6.3.2(3)) and the Jacobian bound in step 5 of the parent proof.
1. Notation. 𝓘 := the strictly increasing maps I : Fin n → Fin P; e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k; for I ∈ 𝓘, α_I := α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I n}); by definition |α|_E = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I²)^{1/2} (the sum over all I with the StrictMono filter). For v = (v_1, …, v_n) let V be the P×n matrix V_{k,j} := ⟨e_k, v_j⟩ = v_j(k), and for I ∈ 𝓘 let V_I be the n×n matrix (V_I)_{a,j} := v_j(I a).
2. Expansion. α(v) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I·det V_I. Proof: write v_j = Σ_k v_j(k)e_k and expand by multilinearity: α(v) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_j v_j(f j))·α(e_{f 1}, …, e_{f n}). Terms with f not injective vanish (α alternating, repeated argument). Each injective f is uniquely f = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 (the increasing enumeration of its range) and σ a permutation, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)α_I. So α(v) = Σ_I α_I Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j v_j(I(σ j)) = Σ_I α_I det V_I by the Leibniz formula.
3. Cauchy–Binet. Σ_{I∈𝓘} (det V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. Proof: det(VᵀV) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i (Σ_k V_{k,i}V_{k,σ i}) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i V_{f i, i})·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{f i, σ i} = Σ_f (Π_i V_{f i, i})·det(V_f), where V_f is the n×n matrix (V_{f a, j})_{a,j}. det V_f = 0 unless f is injective, and for f = I∘σ, det V_f = sgn(σ) det V_I (row permutation). Hence det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det V_I·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{I(σ i), i} = Σ_I (det V_I)² (Leibniz formula again).
4. Part (1). By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘, |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}(Σ_I (det V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩))^{1/2} by step 3 (the Gram determinant is ≥ 0, being a sum of squares).
5. Part (2). For n = 0 take α the constant 0-covector with value 1: |α|_E = 1 (𝓘 consists of the empty map) and α() = 1. For n ≥ 1 let α(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}; it is multilinear, alternating and continuous, hence an n-covector, and α(τ) = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1. Moreover α_I = det(⟨τ_a, e_{I b}⟩)_{a,b} = det(T_I) with T the P×n matrix of τ (transposes have equal determinants), so by step 3 applied to v = τ: |α|_E² = Σ_I det(T_I)² = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = 1. Hence |α|_E = 1 ≤ 1.
6. Degenerate cases are covered: if n > P then 𝓘 = ∅, |α|_E = 0, every n-covector vanishes (n vectors in ℝ^P are dependent) and there is no orthonormal n-family.
proof_key_steps: Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I) det V_I by multilinearity and alternation.
Cauchy–Binet: Σ_I (det V_I)² = det(v_i·v_j).
Cauchy–Schwarz gives (1); the covector u ↦ det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩) gives (2).

subproblems.title: Simon 6.3.2(3): the local mass of an integer multiplicity current is the weight of its varifold
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple representing T. Then for every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n, i.e. T.massOn W = R.measure W (mass computed with the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.3.2(3) (M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W}θ dH^n = μ_V(W)), used in steps 4–5 of the parent proof ("M_W(T) = μ_T(W)"). Write CB for the sibling covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds.
1. Notation. M, θ, ξ as usual; R.measure W = ∫⁻_{M∩W} θ dH^n (withDensity of θ w.r.t. H^n⌞M; W is Borel). An n-form ω is admissible if ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x; by definition T.massOn W = sup over admissible ω of ofReal(T ω).
2. Pointwise bound. For H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ) with τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent plane and s = ±1 (R.orients). Applying CB(1) with v = τ (Gram matrix I, determinant 1): |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ |β|_E for every n-covector β.
3. Upper bound. For admissible ω, T ω = ∫_M θ ξ(ω(x)) dH^n; the integrand vanishes for x ∉ W (ω(x) = 0 there since tsupport ω ⊆ W) and is ≤ θ(x) for a.e. x ∈ M ∩ W by step 2. Hence ofReal(T ω) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩W} θ = R.measure W, and T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W.
4. Reduction for the lower bound. Let W_k := {x : |x| < k and closedBall(x, 1/k) ⊆ W} (k ≥ 1; this also works for W = ℝ^P). W_k is open: if x ∈ W_k, the compact set closedBall(x, 1/k) lies in the open W, so closedBall(x, 1/k + ε) ⊆ W for some ε > 0, and then every y with |y − x| < ε small enough is in W_k. The W_k increase, ⋃_k W_k = W, and closure W_k ⊆ {x : |x| ≤ k, closedBall(x, 1/(k+1)) ⊆ W} ⊆ W_{k+2}, so closure W_k is compact and contained in W_{k+2} ⊆ W. By continuity from below, R.measure W = sup_k R.measure W_k. So it suffices to show T.massOn W ≥ (1 − ε)R.measure(W') for W' := W_k, W'' := W_{k+2} and every ε ∈ (0,1). Note R.measure(W'') < ∞ because closure W'' is a compact subset of W ⊆ U.
5. Measurable near-dual covectors. Let B := {β : |β|_E ≤ 1} in the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors and (β_j) a countable dense subset of B. For a.e. x ∈ M, sup_j ξ(x)(β_j) ≥ 1: by CB(2) there is β with |β|_E ≤ 1 and β(τ) = 1, so ξ(x)(sβ) = 1 with sβ ∈ B, and ξ(x) is a continuous linear functional. Let ξ̃ be a strongly measurable function equal to ξ a.e., j(x) := least j with ξ̃(x)(β_j) > 1 − ε (j(x) := 0 if none), and α(x) := β_{j(x)}. Then α is measurable, α(x) ∈ B for all x, and ξ(x)(α(x)) > 1 − ε for a.e. x ∈ M.
6. Smooth admissible approximants. ν := θ·H^n⌞(M ∩ W'') is a finite Borel measure and f := 1_{W'}·α ∈ L¹(ν; Λ^n) takes values in B. (a) Continuous compactly supported maps ℝ^P → Λ^n are dense in L¹(ν) (ν finite Borel on ℝ^P), so there are g_j → f in L¹(ν) and, after passing to a subsequence, ν-a.e. (b) ρ(v) := v / max(1, |v|_E) is continuous, B-valued and the identity on B, so ρ∘g_j → ρ∘f = f ν-a.e. with |ρ∘g_j|_E ≤ 1; by dominated convergence ρ∘g_j → f in L¹(ν). (c) Take χ ∈ C_c^∞(W''), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on closure W'. Then χ·(ρ∘g_j) is B-valued (B is convex and balanced) and converges to χf = f in L¹(ν). (d) Mollify: with ψ_δ ≥ 0 smooth, ∫ψ_δ = 1, supported in B_δ(0), the forms (χ·ρ∘g_j)∗ψ_δ are smooth, B-valued (averages of B-valued functions, B closed convex), supported in W'' for δ < dist(tsupport χ, ℝ^P ∖ W''), and converge uniformly to χ·ρ∘g_j as δ → 0, hence in L¹(ν). A diagonal choice yields ω_j ∈ 𝒟^n(U), admissible for massOn W (tsupport ω_j ⊆ W'' ⊆ W, |ω_j|_E ≤ 1), with ω_j → f in L¹(ν).
7. Evaluation. T ω_j = ∫_M θ ξ(ω_j) dH^n = ∫ ξ(ω_j) dν (ω_j vanishes off W''). By step 2, |∫ξ(ω_j)dν − ∫ξ(f)dν| ≤ ∫|ω_j − f|_E dν → 0, and ∫ ξ(f) dν = ∫_{M∩W'} θ·ξ(α) dH^n ≥ (1 − ε)·R.measure(W'). Hence T.massOn W ≥ sup_j ofReal(T ω_j) ≥ (1 − ε)R.measure(W'). Letting ε → 0 and then k → ∞ (step 4) gives T.massOn W ≥ R.measure W; with step 3, equality.
proof_key_steps: CB(1) with an orthonormal frame gives |ξ(β)| ≤ |β|_E, hence M_W(T) ≤ ∫_{M∩W}θ.
CB(2) and a countable dense subset of the unit ball give a measurable covector field α with |α|_E ≤ 1 and ξ(α) > 1 − ε.
Approximate 1_{W'}α in L¹(θH^n⌞M) by smooth admissible forms (density, radial retraction, cutoff, mollification) and exhaust W.

subproblems.title: Simon 6.2.23–2.24 and 6.3.3–3.9: push-forward of an integer multiplicity current by a C¹ diffeomorphism
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), K ⊆ U compact, and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ bijection with Dφ(x) injective for every x and φ(x) = x for x ∉ K. Then there is an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with S(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ^#ω(x)) dH^n(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where φ^#ω(x) = ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) is the pulled-back covector (so S = φ_#T), and ∂S = 0 whenever ∂T = 0 (BoundaryVanishes; vacuous for n = 0).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.2.23–2.24 (definition of f_#T, ∂f_# = f_#∂, the integral formula 2.24(2)–(3)) and 6.3.3–3.9 (f_#T is integer multiplicity; for injective f, f_#T = τ(f(M), θ∘f^{-1}, induced orientation), with the induced orientation of 3.5/3.7), together with Ch. 3 §1–2 (approximate tangent planes, area formula); this is step 4 of the parent proof. The printed argument (3.6–3.7) uses without proof that dφ_x maps T_xM onto the approximate tangent plane of φ(M) at φ(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M; steps 4–6 supply this. Notation: E := ℝ^P; M, θ, ξ from R; Q(x) := approxTangentPlane n M x and p(x) its orthogonal projection; for a linear L and a plane Q, J(L, Q) := normDet(L restricted to Q) = (det(Lτ_a·Lτ_b))^{1/2} for any orthonormal basis τ of Q (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet, normDet_sq_eq_det_gram); β∘L denotes β.compContinuousLinearMap L. The argument is uniform in n ≥ 0; step 10 records what each step reduces to when n = 0.
1. φ is a bi-Lipschitz C¹ diffeomorphism preserving U. By the inverse function theorem φ^{-1} is C¹ (Dφ(x) is an injective, hence invertible, endomorphism of E). φ is the identity on the open set E ∖ K, so Dφ = I there, φ(E ∖ K) = E ∖ K, hence (φ bijective) φ(K) = K, φ(U) = U and φ^{-1}(U) = U. Dφ − I and D(φ^{-1}) − I are continuous with compact support, so ‖Dφ‖, ‖D(φ^{-1})‖ ≤ Λ on E for some Λ ≥ 1 and, by the mean value inequality, φ and φ^{-1} are Λ-Lipschitz. Hence Λ^{-n}H^n(A) ≤ H^n(φ(A)) ≤ Λ^n H^n(A) for all A ⊆ E (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le for φ and φ^{-1}; μHE[n] is a fixed positive multiple of μH[n]); in particular φ and φ^{-1} map H^n-null sets to H^n-null sets.
2. S is a current with the stated action. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) let g_ω(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(φx)∘Dφ(x)). For a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) with |τ_i| = 1, so |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm), and ‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖‖L‖^n. g_ω vanishes off C_ω := φ^{-1}(tsupport ω), a compact subset of U, so |g_ω| ≤ Λ^n·sup‖ω‖·θ·1_{C_ω} a.e. on M, which is integrable by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; g_ω is a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable, x ↦ ω(φx) and x ↦ Dφ(x) continuous, evaluation continuous). Define S(ω) := ∫_M g_ω dH^n. S is linear in ω, and if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in one compact C ⊆ U, uniform convergence) then |S(ω_j)| ≤ Λ^n sup‖ω_j‖ ∫_{M∩φ^{-1}C} θ dH^n → 0; so S is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with the required action formula.
3. Boundary. Let n ≥ 1 and T.boundary = 0 (for n = 0, BoundaryVanishes S is True). Fix η ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U). Let ρ_k be smooth mollifiers supported in B_{1/k}(0) and φ_k := id + ρ_k∗(φ − id). Then φ_k is C^∞, φ_k = id outside K_k := K + closedBall(0, 1/k), a compact subset of U for k ≥ k_0, and φ_k → φ, Dφ_k → Dφ uniformly on E. The pulled-back form φ_k^#η(x) := η(φ_k x)∘Dφ_k(x) is smooth with tsupport ⊆ tsupport η ∪ K_k (φ_k = id near every point outside K_k), so φ_k^#η ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U), and d(φ_k^#η) = φ_k^#(dη) (exterior derivative commutes with pull-back by smooth maps: SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with domains univ, i.e. Mathlib extDerivWithin_pullback). Therefore 0 = T.boundary(φ_k^#η) = T(φ_k^#dη) = ∫_M θ ξ(dη(φ_k x)∘Dφ_k(x)) dH^n. As k → ∞ these integrands converge pointwise to θ ξ(dη(φx)∘Dφ(x)) and are dominated by C·θ·1_{tsupport η ∪ K_{k_0}}; by dominated convergence S(dη) = 0. So S.boundary = 0.
4. Lipschitz pieces of M. By R.rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable n M) there are M_0 ⊆ E with H^n(M_0) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j); G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero).
 (a) Coercivity constant. For an injective linear map A : ℝ^n → E define m(A) > 0 as follows. If n ≥ 1, m(A) := min{|Ah| : h ∈ ℝ^n, |h| = 1}; the minimum exists and is positive because the unit sphere of ℝ^n is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and nowhere zero on it. If n = 0, m(A) := 1; the unit sphere of ℝ^0 = {0} is empty, so no minimum is taken. In both cases (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for every h ∈ ℝ^n: for n ≥ 1 and h ≠ 0 apply the definition to h/|h| and multiply by |h|; for h = 0, which is the only vector when n = 0, both sides vanish. (Alternatively, one may take m(A) := 1/K for any K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A, which Mathlib's LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith supplies for every injective A in every dimension, including n = 0; only m(A) > 0 and (†) are used below.)
 (b) Positive radius. Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) > 0, hence r(A) ≠ 0, for every A, including every A when n = 0 (then every A is injective and r(A) = 1/2). This is exactly the hypothesis rpos : ∀ A, r A ≠ 0 of Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt.
 (c) Partition. Apply that theorem with f := F_j, s := G_j, f' := fderiv ℝ F_j (for a ∈ G_j, F_j is differentiable at a, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (DF_j(a)) G_j a) and r from (b). It gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} ⊆ ℝ^n (k ∈ ℕ) with G_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k} and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} such that ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_{j,k} (G_j ∩ t_{j,k}) (r(A_{j,k})), i.e. |F_j(a) − F_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}, and, when G_j ≠ ∅, A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) for some y ∈ G_j; in particular A_{j,k} is injective and r(A_{j,k}) = m(A_{j,k})/2. (When G_j = ∅ all sets G_j ∩ t_{j,k} are empty and are discarded.) By (†), for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}: |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ |A_{j,k}(a − a')| − (m(A_{j,k})/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A_{j,k})/2)|a − a'|. So F_j is bi-Lipschitz on the Borel set G_j ∩ t_{j,k}, with lower constant m(A_{j,k})/2 > 0.
 (d) Disjoint pieces of M. Enumerate the nonempty sets G_j ∩ t_{j,k} as D_i, i ∈ I, where I = {1, 2, …} or I = {1, …, N} is a countable (possibly finite or empty, e.g. always empty when n > P) initial segment of the positive integers, with F_i the corresponding F_j and m_i := m(A_{j,k})/2 > 0: D_i is Borel, F_i is Lipschitz, |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| ≥ m_i|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_i, and F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at each point of D_i. Recursively let B_i := (D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M)) ∖ F_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'})). Images of Borel sets under continuous maps injective on them are Borel (Lusin–Souslin, Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), so by induction on i ∈ I every B_i is Borel and P_i := F_i(B_i) is a Borel subset of M; the P_i are pairwise disjoint by construction. Finally Z := M ∖ ⋃_i P_i ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j) is H^n-null: if x ∈ M ∖ M_0 then x = F_j(a) for some j and a; if a ∉ G_j then x ∈ F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j); if a ∈ G_j then a ∈ D_i for some i with F_i = F_j and a ∈ F_i^{-1}(M), so either a ∈ B_i and x ∈ P_i, or x ∈ F_{i'}(B_{i'}) = P_{i'} for some i' < i.
5. Density lemma. Let Y ⊆ U be Borel with H^n(Y ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U, F : ℝ^n → E Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel, and m > 0 with |F(a) − F(a')| ≥ m|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ B, F(B) ⊆ Y, and F differentiable with injective derivative at each point of B. Then for H^n-a.e. y ∈ F(B), writing y = F(b) (b ∈ B is unique), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y y (range DF(b)). Proof. (i) For H^n-a.e. y ∈ F(B): H^n((Y ∖ F(B)) ∩ B_r(y)) = o(r^n) as r ↓ 0. Indeed, on a compact C ⊆ U with y in its interior, ν := H^n⌞(Y ∩ C) is a finite Borel measure; by the Besicovitch density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div) ν(F(B) ∩ B̄_r(y))/ν(B̄_r(y)) → 1 for ν-a.e. y ∈ F(B), so ν((Y ∖ F(B)) ∩ B̄_r(y)) = o(ν(B̄_r(y))); and ν(B̄_r(y)) ≤ C_n r^n for small r at H^n-a.e. y ∈ Y ∩ C by the upper density theorem applied to the H^n-measurable set A := Y ∩ C of finite measure (Simon Ch. 1 (3.26)(1), SimonGMT ae_hausdorff_dimensionalUpperDensity_le_one with real exponent n ≥ 0, stated for Simon's Hausdorff measure simonHausdorffMeasureReal n; by SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure it is a fixed positive multiple of μHE[n], so the bound holds for μHE[n] with another constant and the exceptional sets have the same null sets). Covering U by countably many such C gives the claim for H^n-a.e. y ∈ F(B). (ii) For f ∈ C_c(E) with support in B_R(0): by scaling of H^n and the injective Lipschitz area formula (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, Jacobian J_F = areaJacobianAt F = normDet DF), ∫_{η_{y,r}(F(B))} f dH^n = r^{-n}∫_B f((F(a) − F(b))/r) J_F(a) da = ∫_{(B−b)/r} f((F(b + rc) − F(b))/r) J_F(b + rc) dc. Only |c| ≤ R/m contributes, before the limit because |F(b + rc) − F(b)| ≥ mr|c| when b + rc ∈ B, and in the limit because |DF(b)c| ≥ m|c| for every c ∈ ℝ^n. For the latter, let b be a Lebesgue density point of B and c ∈ ℝ^n, c ≠ 0: there are r_l ↓ 0 and c_l → c with b + r_l c_l ∈ B (otherwise, for some ε > 0 and all small r, B misses b + r·B_ε(c) ⊆ B_{r(|c|+ε)}(b), a set of measure r^n|B_ε(0)|, a fixed positive fraction of |B_{r(|c|+ε)}(b)|, contradicting density 1); then m r_l|c_l| ≤ |F(b + r_l c_l) − F(b)| = r_l|DF(b)c_l| + o(r_l), and dividing by r_l and letting l → ∞ gives m|c| ≤ |DF(b)c|. Choose b a Lebesgue density point of B and a Lebesgue point of J_F (a.e. b ∈ B; F maps L^n-null sets to H^n-null sets, so the corresponding y form a full-measure subset of F(B)). Then 1_{(B−b)/r} → 1 and J_F(b + r·) → J_F(b) in L¹(B_{R/m}), and (F(b + rc) − F(b))/r → DF(b)c uniformly for |c| ≤ R/m; f is bounded and uniformly continuous, so the integral tends to ∫_{ℝ^n} f(DF(b)c) J_F(b) dc = ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n (linear area formula, Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). (iii) |∫_{η_{y,r}Y} f dH^n − ∫_{η_{y,r}F(B)} f dH^n| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ r^{-n} H^n((Y ∖ F(B)) ∩ B_{rR}(y)) → 0 by (i). As finrank range DF(b) = n (DF(b) is injective), the definition of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt is met.
6. Tangent planes of M and of φ(M). Step 5 with Y := M (Borel, ⊆ U, and H^n(M ∩ C) ≤ ∫_{M∩C} θ dH^n < ∞ for compact C ⊆ U because θ ≥ 1 on M) and the pieces (F_i, B_i, m_i), plus uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), gives Q(F_i b) = range DF_i(b) for L^n-a.e. b ∈ B_i (H^n-null subsets of P_i pull back to L^n-null subsets of B_i because F_i^{-1} is (1/m_i)-Lipschitz on P_i). φ(M) is Borel, ⊆ U, with H^n(φ(M) ∩ C) ≤ Λ^n H^n(M ∩ φ^{-1}C) < ∞ for compact C ⊆ U; φ(M) is the disjoint union of φ(Z) and the (φ∘F_i)(B_i), with H^n(φ(Z)) = 0, and φ∘F_i is Lipschitz, satisfies |φF_i(a) − φF_i(a')| ≥ (m_i/Λ)|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ B_i, and is differentiable at each b ∈ B_i with injective derivative Dφ(F_i b)∘DF_i(b). Step 5 with Y := φ(M) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n φ(M) (φ x) (Dφ(x)(range DF_i(b))) for H^n-a.e. x = F_i(b) ∈ P_i. Since null sets correspond under φ, F_i and their inverses, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M: (★) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n φ(M) φ(x) (Dφ(x)Q(x)).
7. Area formula on M. For every function g : E → [0, ∞] (no measurability of g is needed): ∫_{φ(M)} g dH^n = ∫_M g(φx)J(x) dH^n(x) (lower Lebesgue integrals), J(x) := J(Dφ(x), Q(x)). Both sides split over the disjoint Borel pieces, since Z and φ(Z) are null (Mathlib lintegral_iUnion needs measurable pieces but no measurability of the integrand). On a piece, by the weighted injective Lipschitz area formula for φ∘F_i and then for F_i: ∫_{φ(P_i)} g dH^n = ∫_{B_i} g(φF_ib)·normDet(Dφ(F_ib)∘DF_i(b)) db = ∫_{B_i} g(φF_ib)·normDet(Dφ(F_ib) restricted to range DF_i(b))·normDet(DF_i(b)) db (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp) = ∫_{B_i} (g∘φ·J)(F_ib)·normDet(DF_i(b)) db (step 6, an a.e. equality in b, so lintegral_congr_ae applies) = ∫_{P_i} (g∘φ)·J dH^n; the SimonGMT weighted area formula weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn takes an arbitrary weight g : F → [0, ∞]. subproblems.title: Deformations along a vector field tangent to a C² submanifold (Simon Ch. 2 before 5.8; Ch. 4, 2.5)
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support, spt X ⊆ U and X(x) ∈ T_xN for x ∈ N ∩ U. Then there is a family (φ_t)_{t∈ℝ} of maps ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that every φ_t is C¹, bijective, with injective derivative everywhere, φ_t = id outside spt X and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, and Dφ_t = I + t·DX + o(t) uniformly: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − t·DX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all |t| < δ and all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (X : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ U → (∀ x ∈ N ∩ U, X x ∈ tangentSpace N x) → ∃ φ : ℝ → Euclid P → Euclid P, (∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t) ∧ Bijective (φ t) ∧ (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ (φ t) x)) ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ tsupport X → φ t x = x) ∧ MapsTo (φ t) (N ∩ U) (N ∩ U)) ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, |t| < δ → ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x - ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - t • fderiv ℝ X x‖ ≤ ε * |t|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon asserts the existence of such families in Ch. 2 (discussion before 5.8, families as in 5.6) and Ch. 4, 2.5–2.6; the parent proof (step 3) takes the flow of X. Here the family is built by composing finitely many deformations that are linear in straightening coordinates of N; it has exactly the properties used later (φ_t = id off spt X, φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, Dφ_t = I + tDX + o(t)) and avoids differentiable dependence of ODE solutions on initial data. Write E := ℝ^P, K := tsupport X.
1. Preliminaries. Since (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, N ∩ U = N̄ ∩ U is relatively closed in U, so U ∖ N is open and K ∩ N = K ∩ N̄ is compact. By the sibling chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv, for every chart (V, W, ψ) of N (as in IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N) and v ∈ V, T_{ψ(v)}N = range Dψ(v), a linear subspace of dimension d; in particular X(z) ∈ range Dψ(v) when z = ψ(v) ∈ N ∩ U, and T_zN is closed under linear combinations.
2. Local straightening. Fix p ∈ N and a chart (V, W, ψ), ψ ∈ C²(V), with p = ψ(v_p). Let F_p := (range Dψ(v_p))^⊥ (dimension P − d) and Ψ_p(a, w) := ψ(v_p + a) + w for a ∈ V − v_p, w ∈ F_p. Ψ_p is C² and DΨ_p(0,0)(h, k) = Dψ(v_p)h + k is a linear isomorphism ℝ^d × F_p → E. By the C² inverse function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, ContDiffAt.to_localInverse) there is an open product of balls B_p = B'_p × B''_p ∋ (0,0) on which Ψ_p is injective with invertible derivative, O'_p := Ψ_p(B_p) is open, and the inverse Φ_p : O'_p → B_p is C². As ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto N ∩ W (properness and injectivity, cf. step 3 of the proof of the sibling), ψ(v_p + B'_p) is a relatively open neighbourhood of p in N, so there is ρ > 0 with N ∩ B_ρ(p) ⊆ ψ(v_p + B'_p). Put O_p := O'_p ∩ B_ρ(p) ∩ U ∩ W (if p ∈ U). Then for z ∈ O_p: z ∈ N iff Φ_p(z) ∈ B'_p × {0} (if z ∈ N then z = ψ(v_p + a) = Ψ_p(a, 0) with a ∈ B'_p, and injectivity of Ψ_p on B_p gives Φ_p(z) = (a, 0); conversely Ψ_p(a, 0) = ψ(v_p + a) ∈ N).
3. Local deformations. Let Y ∈ C¹(E; E) with tsupport Y compact ⊆ O_p and Y(z) ∈ T_zN for z ∈ N ∩ O_p. Put Z(b) := DΨ_p(b)^{-1}Y(Ψ_p(b)) for b ∈ B_p and Z := 0 elsewhere; Z is C¹ (DΨ_p is C¹ and invertible on B_p) with compact support Φ_p(tsupport Y) ⊆ B_p. For b = (a, 0) ∈ B_p, Y(Ψ_p(a,0)) ∈ T_{ψ(v_p+a)}N = range Dψ(v_p + a) = DΨ_p(a,0)(ℝ^d × {0}), so Z(a, 0) ∈ ℝ^d × {0}. For |t| < t_Y := 1/(1 + sup‖DZ‖), h_t := id + tZ has ‖Dh_t − I‖ < 1 everywhere, so h_t is a C¹ diffeomorphism of ℝ^d × F_p (Mathlib ApproximatesLinearOn.toHomeomorph with the identity as linear part, plus the inverse function theorem), equal to the identity off tsupport Z; hence it maps tsupport Z and B_p onto themselves, and h_t(a, 0) = (a + tZ_1(a,0), 0) ∈ B'_p × {0} for (a, 0) ∈ B_p. Define φ^Y_t := Ψ_p∘h_t∘Φ_p on O'_p and φ^Y_t := id elsewhere. Since φ^Y_t = id on O'_p ∖ tsupport Y, φ^Y_t is C¹ on E, bijective, with invertible derivative everywhere, equal to id off tsupport Y and mapping tsupport Y ⊆ U onto itself. It maps N ∩ U into N ∩ U: for z ∈ N ∩ O_p, Φ_p(z) ∈ B'_p × {0}, so φ^Y_t(z) ∈ Ψ_p(B'_p × {0}) ⊆ N, and φ^Y_t(z) ∈ tsupport Y ∪ {z} ⊆ U; points of N outside tsupport Y are fixed. Expansion: for y ∈ O'_p and b := Φ_p(y), Dφ^Y_t(y) = DΨ_p(b + tZ(b))(I + tDZ(b))DΨ_p(b)^{-1}. Differentiating Y(Ψ_p(b)) = DΨ_p(b)Z(b) gives DY(y)DΨ_p(b) = D²Ψ_p(b)[·, Z(b)] + DΨ_p(b)DZ(b), and D²Ψ_p is symmetric and uniformly continuous on a compact neighbourhood of tsupport Z, so DΨ_p(b + tZ(b)) = DΨ_p(b) + tD²Ψ_p(b)[Z(b), ·] + o(t) uniformly in b ∈ tsupport Z. Multiplying out, Dφ^Y_t(y) = I + tDY(y) + o(t) uniformly in y ∈ tsupport Y; for y ∉ tsupport Y both sides equal I (φ^Y_t = id near y, DY(y) = 0). Thus sup_y ‖Dφ^Y_t(y) − I − tDY(y)‖ = o(t), and |φ^Y_t(y) − y| ≤ C_Y|t| for all y.
4. Partition of unity. Cover the compact K ∩ N by finitely many O_{p_1}, …, O_{p_m} (p_i ∈ K ∩ N ⊆ U) and put O_0 := U ∖ N (open); then K ⊆ O_0 ∪ O_{p_1} ∪ ⋯ ∪ O_{p_m}. Choose smooth χ_0, …, χ_m with compact tsupport χ_i ⊆ O_{p_i} (tsupport χ_0 ⊆ O_0) and Σ_i χ_i = 1 on a neighbourhood of K (smooth partition of unity subordinate to a finite open cover of a compact set; Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity / exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset). Put X_i := χ_i X. Then X = Σ_i X_i, X_i ∈ C¹_c with tsupport X_i ⊆ tsupport χ_i ∩ K; for i ≥ 1, X_i(z) = χ_i(z)X(z) ∈ T_zN for z ∈ N ∩ O_{p_i}; and X_0 = 0 on N.
5. The family. Let φ^0_t := id + tX_0 and φ^i_t := φ^{X_i}_t (step 3 with p = p_i), and t_0 := min(t_{X_1}, …, t_{X_m}, 1/(1 + sup‖DX_0‖)) > 0. For |t| < t_0 set φ_t := φ^0_t∘φ^1_t∘⋯∘φ^m_t, and φ_t := id for |t| ≥ t_0. For every t: (a) φ_t is C¹, bijective, with invertible (in particular injective) derivative everywhere (φ^0_t by the argument of step 3, compositions of such maps); (b) φ_t(x) = x for x ∉ K, because each factor is the identity outside tsupport X_i ⊆ K; (c) φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, because each φ^i_t (i ≥ 1) maps N ∩ U into itself and φ^0_t fixes every point of N. (d) Expansion: with y_i := φ^{i+1}_t∘⋯∘φ^m_t(x), Dφ_t(x) = Dφ^0_t(y_0)·Dφ^1_t(y_1)⋯Dφ^m_t(x); each factor is I + tDX_i(y_i) + o(t) uniformly (step 3; exact for i = 0), |y_i − x| ≤ C|t|, and the DX_i are uniformly continuous, so DX_i(y_i) = DX_i(x) + o(1) uniformly. Multiplying the finitely many bounded factors, Dφ_t(x) = I + tΣ_i DX_i(x) + o(t) = I + tDX(x) + o(t) uniformly in x: for every ε > 0 there is δ ∈ (0, t_0] with ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all |t| < δ and all x.
proof_key_steps: Straighten N near each point by the C² map (a, w) ↦ ψ(v_p + a) + w and the inverse function theorem.
In straightening coordinates a field tangent to N is horizontal on ℝ^d × {0}, so b ↦ b + tZ(b) preserves N; conjugating gives C¹ diffeomorphisms with Dφ_t = I + tDY + o(t).
A partition of unity splits X into finitely many such pieces plus a piece vanishing on N; composing the deformations gives the family.

subproblems.title: First variation of mass along push-forwards (Simon Ch. 4, 2.2; Ch. 2, 5.3): upper bound
subproblems.statement: Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U ⊆ ℝ^P, W ⊆ ℝ^P open with μ_V(W) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n < ∞, X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support and spt X ⊆ W, and (φ_t)_{t∈ℝ} C¹ maps with φ_t = id outside spt X and ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all x whenever |t| < δ(ε). Then for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that for every |t| < δ and every S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with S(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) dH^n for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U): M_W(S) ≤ μ_V(W) + t·δV(X) + ε|t|, where δV(X) = ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n = R.firstVariation X.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (X : Euclid P → Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen W → R.measure W ≠ ∞ → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ W → (∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t)) → (∀ t x, x ∉ tsupport X → φ t x = x) → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, |t| < δ → ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x - ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - t • fderiv ℝ X x‖ ≤ ε * |t|) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, |t| < δ → ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (φ t x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (φ t) x)) ∂μHE[n]) → S.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((R.measure W).toReal + t * R.firstVariation X + ε * |t|)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 2.2 and Ch. 2, 5.2–5.3 (the area formula expresses the mass of φ_{t#} as ∫ θJ^Mφ_t and J^Mφ_t = 1 + t div_M X + o(t)); this is step 5 of the parent proof, in the one-sided form that suffices for minimality. Write CB for the sibling covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds and TM for the sibling imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm. Notation: K := tsupport X ⊆ W, Q(x) := approxTangentPlane n M x, p(x) its projection, div_M X(x) := tangentialDivergence n M X x = trace(p(x)DX(x)), m := (R.measure W).toReal = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n, A := sup_x ‖DX(x)‖ < ∞, and R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n.
1. Good points. For H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal basis τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) of an approximate tangent plane and s = ±1 with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ) for all n-covectors β (R.orients); by uniqueness that plane is Q(x), and then div_M X(x) = Σ_a τ_a·DX(x)τ_a (trace of p(x)DX(x) computed in an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P adapted to Q(x)).
2. Jacobian inequality. For a linear map L and orthonormal τ_1, …, τ_n let G := (Lτ_a·Lτ_b)_{a,b}, a positive semidefinite matrix. If λ_1, …, λ_n ≥ 0 are its eigenvalues then det G = Πλ_a ≤ Π e^{λ_a − 1} = exp(tr G − n) (as λ ≤ e^{λ−1}), and tr G = Σ_a |Lτ_a|². Take L = I + tDX(x) + E with ‖E‖ ≤ η|t|, η ≤ 1, |t| ≤ 1. Then |Lτ_a|² = 1 + 2tτ_a·DX(x)τ_a + 2τ_a·Eτ_a + |tDX(x)τ_a + Eτ_a|² ≤ 1 + 2tτ_a·DX(x)τ_a + 2η|t| + (A + 1)²t², so (det G)^{1/2} ≤ exp(σ) with σ := t·div + nη|t| + n(A+1)²t²/2, where div := Σ_a τ_a·DX(x)τ_a. Put c_0 := (n + 1)(A + 2 + (A+1)²) > 0. Then |σ| ≤ |t|c_0 ≤ 1 for |t| ≤ 1/c_0, and e^σ ≤ 1 + σ + σ² for |σ| ≤ 1, so: (det G)^{1/2} ≤ 1 + t·div + |t|(nη + n(A+1)²|t|/2 + c_0²|t|). Hence, given ε' > 0, choosing η := min(1, ε'/(2n + 1)) and then |t| small, (det G)^{1/2} ≤ 1 + t·div + ε'|t| uniformly in x and τ. (For n = 0 both sides reduce to det of the empty matrix, 1 ≤ 1 + ε'|t|.)
3. Choice of δ. Given ε > 0 put ε' := ε/(m + 1), η as in step 2, and choose δ ∈ (0, 1] with δ ≤ δ(η) from the hypothesis, δ ≤ 1/c_0, δ·(n(A+1)²/2 + c_0²) ≤ ε'/2 and δ·(nA + ε') ≤ 1, so that step 2 yields (det G)^{1/2} ≤ 1 + t·div + ε'|t| for |t| < δ (and 1 + t·div_M X + ε'|t| ≥ 0).
4. Pointwise bound. Fix |t| < δ, S as in the statement and an admissible ω (ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)|_E ≤ 1 for all y). Let g(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)), so S(ω) = ∫_M g dH^n. At a good point x ∈ M ∩ W: g(x) = sθ(x)·ω(φ_t x)(Dφ_t(x)τ_1, …, Dφ_t(x)τ_n), so by CB(1) and step 2 (with L = Dφ_t(x), E := Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x), ‖E‖ ≤ η|t|): |g(x)| ≤ θ(x)·|ω(φ_t x)|_E·(det G)^{1/2} ≤ θ(x)(1 + t·div_M X(x) + ε'|t|). At a good point x ∈ M ∖ W: x ∉ K, so φ_t(x) = x ∉ W ⊇ tsupport ω and g(x) = 0. Hence g ≤ h a.e. on M, where h := 1_W·θ·(1 + t·div_M X + ε'|t|).
5. Integration. g is a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable, x ↦ ω(φ_t x) continuous, x ↦ fderiv ℝ (φ_t) x measurable by Mathlib measurable_fderiv) and |g| ≤ θ·1_W·(1 + |t|(nA + ε')), which is integrable because ∫_{M∩W} θ = m < ∞; h is integrable because div_M X is H^n⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (TM: it is the trace of p(x)∘DX(x), a continuous function of (p(x), DX(x))) and bounded by nA. Therefore S(ω) ≤ ∫_M h dH^n = m + t∫_{M∩W} θ div_M X dH^n + ε'|t|m. Since DX(x) = 0 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K, div_M X vanishes off K ⊆ W, so ∫_{M∩W} θ div_M X = R.firstVariation X. With ε'm ≤ ε: S(ω) ≤ m + t·R.firstVariation X + ε|t|.
6. Conclusion. ofReal is monotone, so ofReal(S ω) ≤ ofReal(m + t·R.firstVariation X + ε|t|) for every admissible ω, and taking the supremum, S.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((R.measure W).toReal + t·R.firstVariation X + ε|t|).

subproblems.title: Simon 7.1.2, first claim: a minimizing current in N ∩ U has varifold stationary in N ∩ U
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in N ∩ U (Simon 7.1.1, integer multiplicity competitors) with ∂T = 0 in U (vacuous for n = 0), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T with H^n(M ∖ N) = 0. Then v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U: ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n = 0 for every X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P) with X(x) ∈ T_xN for all x ∈ N ∩ U (R.IsStationaryAlong N).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → IsMinimizingIn T (N ∩ U) → BoundaryVanishes T → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ N) = 0 → R.IsStationaryAlong N
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.1.2 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 29–60) with README erratum 1, i.e. steps 1 and 3–5 of the parent proof; the hypothesis H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 is the consequence of spt T ⊆ N established in step 2 of the parent proof (sibling imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null). Siblings used: imrep_represents_massOn_eq_measure (MASS), imrep_c1_diffeo_pushforward_im (PUSH), tangential_c1_deformation_exists (DEFORM), pushforward_action_massOn_le_first_variation (EXPAND).
1. Fix X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ U and X(x) ∈ tangentSpace N x for x ∈ N ∩ U. Put K := tsupport X (compact, ⊆ U) and δV(X) := R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n. We show δV(X) = 0.
2. Case n = 0. approxTangentPlane 0 M x has finrank 0, hence equals ⊥, for every x (in both branches of its definition), so its projection is 0 and tangentialDivergence 0 M X x = trace 0 = 0; thus δV(X) = 0. (This is consistent with step 1 of the parent proof, which shows moreover M = ∅.) Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
3. Choice of W. As K is compact in the open U, there is an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U (a small open thickening of K). Then R.measure W ≤ ∫_{M∩closure W} θ dH^n < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult), and by MASS, T.massOn W = R.measure W. Put m := (R.measure W).toReal, so R.measure W = ofReal m.
4. Degenerate case m = 0. Then H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M). For x ∉ K, DX(x) = 0 (X vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K), so tangentialDivergence n M X x = 0. Hence the integrand of δV(X) vanishes H^n⌞M-a.e. and δV(X) = 0. Assume m > 0.
5. Deformations. DEFORM (applied to U, N, X) gives φ : ℝ → ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that for every t: φ_t is C¹, bijective, with injective derivative, φ_t = id off K and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U; and (D): for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all |t| < δ and all x. Since φ_t is a bijection fixing every point of ℝ^P ∖ K, it maps ℝ^P ∖ K onto itself and hence K onto K.
6. Competitors. For each t, PUSH (with U, T, R, K and φ_t) gives an integer multiplicity S_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with BoundaryVanishes S_t (because BoundaryVanishes T) and S_t(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) dH^n for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
7. S_t is admissible in 7.1.1 with this W. (a) W is open and CompactlyContained W U; S_t is integer multiplicity. (b) SameBoundary S_t T: n ≥ 1 and S_t.boundary = 0 = T.boundary. (c) spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N. K ∩ N is compact: N ∩ U = N̄ ∩ U by (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, so K ∩ N = K ∩ N̄ is closed in the compact K. Let y ∈ U ∖ (K ∩ N); choose r > 0 with closedBall(y, r) ⊆ U and closedBall(y, r) ∩ K ∩ N = ∅, and W_y := ball(y, r) (open, closure compact ⊆ U). For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W_y, using T ω = R.action ω: (S_t − T)(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)[ξ(x)(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) − ξ(x)(ω(x))] dH^n; the two integrals may be merged because both integrands are integrable (each is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by C·θ on a compact subset of U — φ_t^{-1}(tsupport ω), resp. tsupport ω — and vanishes elsewhere, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ a.e.; R.locallyIntegrable_mult). The bracket vanishes for x ∈ M ∖ K (φ_t = id on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K, so φ_t x = x and Dφ_t(x) = I); it vanishes for x ∈ M ∩ K ∩ N, because x and φ_t(x) both lie in K ∩ N (step 5: φ_t(K) = K, φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U) where ω vanishes; and M ∩ K ∖ N is H^n-null by hypothesis. So S_t − T vanishes on W_y and y ∈ zeroRegion(S_t − T). Hence spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N ⊆ (N ∩ U) ∩ W. (d) spt(S_t − T) is compact: it is relatively closed in U (complement of the open zeroRegion) and contained in the compact set K ∩ N ⊆ U, so it equals (K ∩ N) ∩ F for a closed F.
   Therefore IsMinimizingIn T (N ∩ U) gives T.massOn W ≤ S_t.massOn W, i.e. ofReal m ≤ S_t.massOn W, for every t ∈ ℝ.
8. First variation bound. EXPAND (with W open, R.measure W ≠ ∞, X C¹ with compact support, K ⊆ W, φ_t C¹, φ_t = id off K, and (D)) gives: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that S_t.massOn W ≤ ofReal(m + t·δV(X) + ε|t|) for all |t| < δ (S_t satisfies the action formula required there).
9. Conclusion. Suppose a := δV(X) ≠ 0. Take ε := |a|/2, δ from step 8, and t := −s·sign(a) with 0 < s < δ and s|a|/2 < m. Then m + ta + ε|t| = m − s|a|/2 ∈ (0, m), and steps 7–8 give ofReal m ≤ S_t.massOn W ≤ ofReal(m − s|a|/2) < ofReal m, a contradiction. Hence δV(X) = R.firstVariation X = 0. As X was arbitrary, R.IsStationaryAlong N.
proof_key_steps: n = 0 is trivial (0-dimensional approximate tangent planes); otherwise fix X tangent to N and W ⊂⊂ U containing spt X, with M_W(T) = μ_V(W).
The deformations φ_t (DEFORM) push T forward to integer multiplicity competitors S_t (PUSH) with ∂S_t = 0 and spt(S_t − T) ⊆ spt X ∩ N compact, using H^n(M ∖ N) = 0.
Minimality gives μ_V(W) ≤ M_W(S_t) ≤ μ_V(W) + tδV(X) + ε|t| (EXPAND) for all small t of both signs, forcing δV(X) = 0.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of a set lying H^n-almost entirely in a C¹ submanifold are contained in its tangent spaces
subproblems.statement: Let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded C¹ d-dimensional submanifold, M ⊆ ℝ^P with H^n(M ∖ N) = 0, and x ∈ N. If Q is an approximate tangent plane of M at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4), then Q ⊆ T_xN (tangentSpace N x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (N M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N → x ∈ N → μHE[n] (M \ N) = 0 → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ⊆ tangentSpace N x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof ("T_xM is contained in T_xN", Simon Ch. 3 §1 and Ch. 2 §4; used in Ch. 4, 2.7 and Ch. 2, 5.9).
1. Chart and tangent space. Since x ∈ N, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N gives a chart (V, W, ψ) with x ∈ W, ψ ∈ C¹(V) injective, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, proper relative to (V, W), Dψ injective on V; write x = ψ(v). By the sibling chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv (r = 1), T := tangentSpace N x = range Dψ(v), a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. Flatness of N at x. For every ε > 0 there is ρ > 0 with dist(z − x, T) ≤ ε|z − x| for all z ∈ N ∩ B_ρ(x). Indeed, as in the proof of the sibling: for z ∈ N close to x we have z ∈ W ∩ N, z = ψ(β) with β ∈ V and β → v as z → x (properness and injectivity); writing ψ(β) − x = Dψ(v)(β − v) + r(β) with |r(β)| ≤ η(|β − v|)|β − v| and using |Dψ(v)h| ≥ c|h|, we get |β − v| ≤ (2/c)|z − x| for z close to x, hence dist(z − x, T) ≤ |r(β)| ≤ (2/c)η(|β − v|)|z − x|, and η(|β − v|) → 0.
3. Suppose Q ⊄ T. Pick q ∈ Q ∖ T; as Q and T are linear subspaces we may assume |q| = 1. Let δ := dist(q, T) ∈ (0, 1] and f(y) := max(0, δ/2 − |y − q|), a nonnegative continuous function with compact support in closedBall(q, δ/2) and f(q) > 0. Every y with f(y) ≠ 0 satisfies |y| ≤ 2 and dist(y, T) ≥ δ/2.
4. ∫_Q f dH^n > 0: f > 0 on the relatively open subset Q ∩ B_{δ/2}(q) ∋ q of Q, and H^n⌞Q has support Q (SimonGMT support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, finrank Q = n).
5. ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n = 0 for all small r > 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x). (a) η_{x,r} is an injective similarity, so H^n(η_{x,r}(M ∖ N)) = r^{-n}H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 and the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M ∩ N) differ by an H^n-null set; hence their restricted measures coincide. (b) Let ε := δ/8, ρ as in step 2 and 0 < r < ρ/2. If y = (z − x)/r with z ∈ N and f(y) ≠ 0, then |z − x| = r|y| ≤ 2r < ρ, so dist(y, T) = dist(z − x, T)/r ≤ ε|z − x|/r ≤ 2ε = δ/4 < δ/2, a contradiction. So f = 0 on η_{x,r}(M ∩ N), and the integral vanishes.
6. By HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0; by step 5 the limit is 0, contradicting step 4. Hence Q ⊆ T = tangentSpace N x.
proof_key_steps: tangentSpace N x = range Dψ(v) (sibling), and N is flat at x: dist(z − x, T_xN) = o(|z − x|) along N.
A test function supported near a unit vector q ∈ Q ∖ T_xN sees no mass of the blow-ups of M ∩ N, and M ∖ N is H^n-null.
Hence its integral over Q, which is positive, would vanish; so Q ⊆ T_xN.

subproblems.title: The tangent-plane projection of a C² submanifold extends to a C¹ field on a neighbourhood
subproblems.statement: Let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold. Then there are an open set O ⊇ N and a map pr : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), C¹ on O, with pr(z) equal to the orthogonal projection onto span(T_zN) (= T_zN) for every z ∈ N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → ∃ (O : Set (Euclid P)) (pr : Euclid P → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)), IsOpen O ∧ N ⊆ O ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 pr O ∧ ∀ z ∈ N, pr z = (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace N z)).starProjection
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (P_N(z) is C¹ along a C² submanifold) and step 6 of the parent proof, where the C¹ field P(π(·)) is used (π the nearest point projection); here any C¹ extension of P_N serves and is built from local charts and a partition of unity.
1. Projection along charts. For z ∈ N let P_N(z) := starProjection(span ℝ (tangentSpace N z)). For a chart (V, W, ψ) of N and v ∈ V, the sibling chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv gives tangentSpace N (ψ v) = range Dψ(v), a linear subspace, so span(tangentSpace N (ψ v)) = range Dψ(v) and P_N(ψ(v)) = Γ(Dψ(v)), where for injective linear L : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, Γ(L) := L(L*L)^{-1}L* is the orthogonal projection onto range L. Γ is C^∞ on the open set of injective linear maps (inversion is smooth).
2. Local extensions. Fix p ∈ N and a chart (V, W, ψ), ψ ∈ C²(V), with p = ψ(v_p). Let F_p := (range Dψ(v_p))^⊥ and Ψ_p(a, w) := ψ(v_p + a) + w (a ∈ V − v_p, w ∈ F_p); Ψ_p is C² with DΨ_p(0,0)(h, k) = Dψ(v_p)h + k invertible. By the C² inverse function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, ContDiffAt.to_localInverse) there is an open product of balls B_p = B'_p × B''_p ∋ (0,0) on which Ψ_p is injective, O'_p := Ψ_p(B_p) is open and the inverse Φ_p : O'_p → B_p is C². As ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto N ∩ W (proper, injective, continuous), there is ρ > 0 with N ∩ B_ρ(p) ⊆ ψ(v_p + B'_p). Put O_p := O'_p ∩ B_ρ(p) ∩ W. For z ∈ N ∩ O_p: z = ψ(v_p + a) = Ψ_p(a, 0) with a ∈ B'_p, so Φ_p(z) = (a, 0). Define Π_p(y) := Γ(Dψ(v_p + π_1(Φ_p(y)))) for y ∈ O_p, where π_1(a, w) := a. Since Φ_p is C², Dψ is C¹ (ψ ∈ C²) with injective values on V, and Γ is smooth, Π_p is C¹ on O_p; and for z ∈ N ∩ O_p, Π_p(z) = Γ(Dψ(v_p + a)) = P_N(ψ(v_p + a)) = P_N(z) by step 1.
3. Gluing. O := ⋃_{p∈N} O_p is open and contains N. As an open subset of ℝ^P, O is a σ-compact (Hausdorff) smooth manifold, and (O_p)_{p∈N} is an open cover of O. Apply Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate on the manifold O with the closed set s := O (all of the manifold): this gives a smooth partition of unity (λ_i)_{i∈I} on O with values in [0,1], tsupport λ_i ⊆ O_{p(i)}, locally finite, and Σ_i λ_i = 1 at every point of O. (Equivalently, one may note that N is closed in O — each N ∩ W_p = ψ_p(V_p) is closed in W_p by properness and O_p ⊆ W_p — but only Σ_i λ_i = 1 on N is used below.) Define pr(y) := Σ_i λ_i(y)Π_{p(i)}(y) for y ∈ O (the term is taken to be 0 where λ_i(y) = 0; near each point only finitely many terms are nonzero, and each nonzero term is C¹ on a neighbourhood) and pr(y) := 0 for y ∉ O. Then pr is C¹ on O.
4. On N. For z ∈ N, only indices with z ∈ tsupport λ_i ⊆ O_{p(i)} contribute, and for them Π_{p(i)}(z) = P_N(z) by step 2; hence pr(z) = (Σ_i λ_i(z))P_N(z) = P_N(z) = (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace N z)).starProjection. (If N = ∅ take O = ∅, pr = 0.)
proof_key_steps: Along a chart, P_N(ψ(v)) = Γ(Dψ(v)) with Γ(L) = L(L*L)^{-1}L* smooth, since T_{ψ(v)}N = range Dψ(v).
Straightening by (a, w) ↦ ψ(v_p + a) + w and the C² inverse function theorem give C¹ local extensions Π_p near each p ∈ N.
A smooth partition of unity on O = ⋃O_p glues them into a C¹ field equal to P_N on N.

subproblems.title: Simon Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14: stationarity in N ∩ U gives locally bounded generalized mean curvature
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U with H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 whose varifold v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U (R.IsStationaryAlong N). Then v(M, θ) has a generalized mean curvature H in U (Simon Ch. 4, 3.14): H is μ_V-measurable, bounded on every compact subset of U, and ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n = −∫ X·H dμ_V for every X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P), μ_V = θH^n⌞M (R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ N) = 0 → R.IsStationaryAlong N → R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14 with Ch. 2, 5.9 (div_M X = div_M X^T − X·H_N), i.e. step 6 of the parent proof. Siblings: chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv (TS), imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm (TM), approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace (H1), submanifold_tangentProjection_c1_extension (EXT).
1. Notation. μ := μHE[n].restrict M, μ_V := R.measure = θ·μ, p(x) := starProjection(approxTangentPlane n M x), div_M Y(x) := tangentialDivergence n M Y x = trace(p(x)∘DY(x)). N ∩ U = N̄ ∩ U (from (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅) is relatively closed in U and Borel. By TS, tangentSpace N z is a linear subspace for z ∈ N, so span(tangentSpace N z) = tangentSpace N z.
2. Extension. EXT gives an open O ⊇ N and pr, C¹ on O, with pr(z) = P_N(z) := starProjection(tangentSpace N z) for z ∈ N; P_N(z) is self-adjoint, idempotent, with range tangentSpace N z.
3. Definition of H. H(x) := Σ_{j=1}^P (Dpr(x)[p(x)e_j])*(p(x)e_j) for x ∈ N ∩ U, and H(x) := 0 otherwise; here Dpr(x) = fderiv ℝ pr x : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), (·)* is the adjoint and (e_j) the standard basis. (At the good points of step 6 this is Σ_i B_x(τ_i, τ_i), the trace over T_xM of the second fundamental form of N, as in the parent proof; this identification is not needed.)
4. Measurability. x ↦ fderiv ℝ pr x is measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv); x ↦ p(x) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (TM); (A, q) ↦ Σ_j (A(qe_j))*(qe_j) is continuous; N ∩ U is Borel. Hence H is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable (μ_V ≪ μ).
5. Local bound. Let K ⊆ U be compact. K ∩ N is compact (relatively closed in K) and contained in O, where Dpr is continuous (pr is C¹ on the open set O), so Λ_0 := sup_{K∩N} ‖Dpr‖ < ∞. For x ∈ K ∩ N, ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Σ_j ‖Dpr(x)‖·|p(x)e_j|² ≤ PΛ_0; for x ∈ K ∖ N, H(x) = 0. So ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Λ := PΛ_0 for every x ∈ K, in particular μ_V-a.e. on K.
6. Good points. G := {x ∈ M ∩ N ∩ U : ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q}. μ(M ∖ G) = 0, because M ⊆ U, μHE[n](M ∖ N) = 0 and R.orients provides approximate tangent planes μ-a.e. For x ∈ G, Q(x) := approxTangentPlane n M x is an approximate tangent plane of M at x, and by H1 (N is in particular an embedded C¹ submanifold, as C² charts are C¹) Q(x) ⊆ tangentSpace N x; thus P_N(x)u = u for u ∈ Q(x).
7. Tangential part. Fix X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U; K_X := tsupport X. K_X ∩ N is compact and ⊆ O ∩ U (open), so there is χ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, tsupport χ ⊆ O ∩ U and χ = 1 on an open neighbourhood V_X of K_X ∩ N. Let X^T(y) := χ(y)·pr(y)(X(y)). X^T is C¹ on O (products and compositions of C¹ maps) and vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport χ; these two open sets cover ℝ^P, so X^T is C¹, with compact support and tsupport X^T ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ U. For z ∈ N ∩ U, X^T(z) = χ(z)P_N(z)X(z) ∈ tangentSpace N z. Hence R.IsStationaryAlong N gives R.firstVariation X^T = 0.
8. Normal part. Y := X − X^T is C¹ with compact support. Claim: for x ∈ G, div_M Y(x) = −⟨X(x), H(x)⟩. Write p := p(x); trace(p∘DY(x)) = trace(p∘DY(x)∘p) = Σ_j ⟨pe_j, DY(x)(pe_j)⟩. (a) If x ∉ K_X: X ≡ 0 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K_X ∋ x, so X^T ≡ 0 there, DY(x) = 0 and X(x) = 0; both sides vanish. (b) If x ∈ K_X: then x ∈ K_X ∩ N ⊆ V_X, and on the open set V_X ∩ O ∋ x, Y(y) = X(y) − pr(y)(X(y)); so DY(x)h = DX(x)h − (Dpr(x)h)(X(x)) − pr(x)(DX(x)h). For u ∈ Q(x) ⊆ tangentSpace N x: ⟨u, DX(x)u − P_N(x)DX(x)u⟩ = ⟨u − P_N(x)u, DX(x)u⟩ = 0, hence ⟨u, DY(x)u⟩ = −⟨u, (Dpr(x)u)X(x)⟩ = −⟨(Dpr(x)u)*u, X(x)⟩. Summing over u = pe_j gives div_M Y(x) = −⟨Σ_j (Dpr(x)[pe_j])*(pe_j), X(x)⟩ = −⟨X(x), H(x)⟩, since x ∈ N ∩ U.
9. Integral identity. All integrands are μ-a.e. strongly measurable (TM for the divergences, step 4 for H) and bounded by a constant times θ·1_{K'} for the compact set K' := K_X ∪ tsupport χ ⊆ U, hence μ-integrable (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). As DX = DX^T + DY and the trace is linear, R.firstVariation X = R.firstVariation X^T + ∫_M θ div_M Y dH^n = 0 − ∫_M θ⟨X, H⟩ dH^n (step 8, μ-a.e.) = −∫ ⟨X, H⟩ dμ_V (integral against the density θ). Together with steps 4 and 5 this is R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature. (For n = 0, p ≡ 0, so H = 0 and both sides vanish.)
proof_key_steps: Extend P_N to a C¹ field pr near N (EXT) and set X^T := χ·pr·X, a C¹_c(U) field tangent to N, so δV(X^T) = 0 by stationarity.
At a.e. x ∈ M (x ∈ N, T_xM ⊆ T_xN by H1) div_M(X − X^T)(x) = −X(x)·H(x) with H(x) = Σ_j (Dpr(x)[p e_j])*(p e_j).
H is measurable (TM) and bounded on compact subsets of U (continuity of Dpr on the compact K ∩ N); integrate to get δV(X) = −∫X·H dμ_V.
